options.title: FRET species — help
options.text:
# FRET species decay

A labeling state (donor-only, FRET pair, or acceptor-only) produces **coupled, different** decays per detection channel:

- **green** (donor emission, donor excitation) — donor decay, FRET-quenched in a DA pair.
- **red** (acceptor emission, donor excitation) — the FRET-*sensitized* acceptor (its rise is shaped by the donor decay), plus donor leakage (α) and directly-excited acceptor (δ).
- **yellow** (acceptor emission, acceptor excitation) — the acceptor's own decay.

## FRET input
Either a **transfer efficiency E**, or a **distributed distance** (Gaussian components: mean R, σ, fraction) + Förster radius R0 (κ²) — the same distance model as the TCSPC FRET fits. **x(D-only)** is the donor-only fraction within the DA population.

## Crosstalk (α/β/γ/δ)
Hellenkamp factors: α = donor leakage into red, δ = direct acceptor excitation, γ = detection/QY ratio, β = excitation-flux ratio. These drive the full **excitation** and **emission** matrices that set the relative channel amplitudes. **Seed from calibration** fills them from the selected detector setup.

## Anisotropy
Per-chromophore r(t) = (r0−r∞)·e^(−t/ρ)+r∞. With **Polarized** on, each channel splits into ∥/⊥ (G-factor corrects ⊥ detection).

## IRF & convolution
The per-channel IRF comes from its **Detector settings** (normalized to unity). The **Laser period** (periodic convolution) and **colour shift** are per-component.

## Fractions
Each labeling state is **one component** — the fFCS filters recover the populations, so no fractions are entered here.

The preview overlays the ideal green/red/yellow decays live.

sections.label: State
sections.description: Which labeling state this component represents.

columns.label: Amplitude
columns.description: Relative weight of this donor lifetime.

columns.label: Lifetime (ns)
columns.description: Donor lifetime in the absence of FRET.

buttons.description: Remove the last donor lifetime component.

columns.label: Amplitude
columns.description: Relative weight of this acceptor lifetime.

buttons.description: Remove the last acceptor lifetime component.

sections.label: Mode
sections.description: Specify FRET by efficiency, or physically by a distributed distance + Förster radius.

rows.label: κ²
rows.description: Orientation factor (distance mode); 2/3 for free rotation.

rows.label: x(D-only)
rows.description: Donor-only fraction within the DA population (no acceptor / no transfer).

columns.label: Mean R (Å)
columns.description: Mean donor-acceptor distance of this Gaussian.

columns.label: σ (Å)
columns.description: Width (σ) of this Gaussian distance component.

columns.label: Fraction
columns.description: Relative weight of this distance component.

rows.label: α leakage
rows.description: Donor bleedthrough into the acceptor (red) channel.

rows.label: δ direct exc.
rows.description: Direct acceptor excitation by the donor-excitation laser.

buttons.label: 📥 Seed from calibration
buttons.description: Fill α/β/γ/δ and R0 from the selected detector-setup calibration.

sections.label: Polarized (∥/⊥)
sections.description: Split each channel into parallel/perpendicular using the anisotropy r(t) = Σ bᵢ·exp(-t/ρᵢ) + r∞.

columns.label: Donor bᵢ
columns.description: Amplitude of this donor anisotropy component.

columns.label: ρ (ns)
columns.description: Donor rotational correlation time of this component.

buttons.description: Remove the last donor rotational component.

columns.label: Acc. bᵢ
columns.description: Amplitude of this acceptor anisotropy component (also used for sensitized emission).

columns.label: ρ (ns)
columns.description: Acceptor rotational correlation time of this component.

buttons.description: Remove the last acceptor rotational component.

sections.title: Histogram & convolution

rows.label: Laser period (ns)
rows.description: Repetition period for periodic convolution (e.g. 12.5 ns at 80 MHz); 0 = aperiodic.

rows.label: Colour shift (ns)
rows.description: Sub-bin periodic IRF colour shift applied to every channel.

sections.description: The per-channel IRF itself comes from the Detector settings; these set the periodic (laser-period) convolution and colour shift.

sections.title: Coupled channel decays
sections.description: Green / red / yellow (and ∥/⊥) decays for this labeling state.
